name: experiment.completed length_lt cap AND no iteration in flight → spawn next autoresearch-propose (continue)
description:
ADR-042 §Phase 2 redesign autoresearch pack — iteration LOOP continue half. Fires on the RUN entity (the coordinator's loop entity, where rule 04 accumulates autoresearch.experiment.completed triples via subject override) when the counter length is strictly less than the iteration cap AND no propose+execute iteration is currently in flight. Spawns the next autoresearch-propose loop.

Iteration-in-flight toggle (2026-06-03 fix for gh#192, with refinement for the self-write-revision filter): the framework's stateful rule evaluator filters self-write replays (ev.Revision > prevState.SourceRevision check), so a rule that toggles its own conditions via its own action does NOT see the resulting Exited transition. To make rule 05's conditions oscillate, the in_flight flag is written by OTHER rules:

- rule 01 (coordinator → autoresearch): stamps in_flight=false (initialize at chain start)
- rule 03 (propose → execute): stamps in_flight=true on the run entity via subject-override (external write from rule 05's perspective, so rule 05 properly Exits)
- rule 04a (execute clean completion): stamps in_flight=false on the run entity (so rule 05 re-Enters and spawns the next iteration)
- rule 04b (execute loop-failed): stamps in_flight=false on the run entity (so the chain continues iterating even after a failed execute — see gh#193 for the consecutive-failure circuit-breaker follow-up)

Rule 05's actions do NOT write in_flight directly. This rule fires, spawns propose, and waits for rule 03 (external writer) to flip the flag. Between rule 05 firing and rule 03 firing (~one propose loop's worth of LLM time), no run-entity update happens — rule 05 doesn't re-fire because there's nothing for it to evaluate against.

This rule ALSO handles iteration 1 (rule 02 baseline→propose was retired in the same fix; it overlapped with this rule's iter-1 spawn and produced the gh#189 duplicate propose). Rule 01 stamps in_flight=false; once baseline completes emit_autoresearch_baseline (which stamps run.status=active + cap + ...), all four conditions become true together → Entered → spawn propose iteration 1.

Note: this rule fires ON the RUN entity, NOT on the firing execute entity. The run entity carries role=coordinator (the run entity IS the coordinator's loop); the role condition reads as 'the run entity'. The substitution $entity.triple.autoresearch.cap reads the cap that emit_autoresearch_baseline stamped onto the run entity during baseline phase.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.autoresearch-propose
on_enter.prompt:
AUTORESEARCH PROPOSE — iteration $entity.triple.autoresearch.experiment.completed.length + 1 of $entity.triple.autoresearch.cap.

A prior iteration's execute loop completed; the run entity's iteration counter is below cap, so you spawn for the next iteration. The run entity at $entity.instance carries the full run state: command, surface, cap, metric_parser, baseline.value, best.value, best.experiment_id, and one autoresearch.experiment.completed triple per iteration so far.

Your prior-iteration context arrives inlined via ADR-048 .triples substitution:

```
$entity.triple.autoresearch.experiment.completed.triples
```

That token resolves to a JSON-encoded array of execute loop IDs for every iteration completed so far. Parse the array; for each ID, call read_loop_result to read that iteration's reason field (carries: hypothesis, value, pass, outcome). Use that journal to:

1. Avoid re-proposing changes that already reverted in a prior iteration.
2. Build on changes that were kept (which became the new running-best — best.value is $entity.triple.autoresearch.best.value).
3. Identify directions the journal suggests have headroom.

Iteration 1 — read the journal as described above. Also read the run entity's current best via the substitutions in your prompt: command is $entity.triple.autoresearch.command; surface is $entity.triple.autoresearch.surface; best.value is $entity.triple.autoresearch.best.value.

Iteration 2 — write your hypothesis to scratchpad. Concrete (file + change pattern + prediction). Within surface. Single-axis. Will not break the pass gate.

Iteration 3 — bash: apply the diff. Verify with `git diff --stat` that changes are scoped within surface.

Iteration 4 — decide(action="measure", reason="<hypothesis + diff summary>"). Rule 03 spawns execute next.

If the journal shows the metric has plateaued (last 3+ iterations all reverted with no kept) AND you have no novel hypothesis to try, decide(action="needs_clarification", reason="plateau observed after $entity.triple.autoresearch.experiment.completed.length iterations; running best=$entity.triple.autoresearch.best.value vs baseline=$entity.triple.autoresearch.baseline.value; no new hypothesis viable"). The recovery rule routes to coordinator, which can call respond_direct with the run's current state — soft stop because v1 substrate does not implement plateau-N as a stop condition. (See pack README §Open substrate questions #1.)

Per ADR-041 addendum 2026-05-15: chain agents do not query the graph. read_loop_result + bash + the .triples substitution are your only read channels.

metadata.fires_on_run_entity: Subscribes to the run entity (the coordinator's loop entity, role=coordinator). Rule 04 stamps autoresearch.experiment.completed ON the run entity (via subject override); when the counter changes, rule 05 evaluates length_lt cap. Mutually exclusive with rule 06 (length_eq cap) — exactly one of the two fires per counter change.
metadata.length_lt_operator_requires: semstreams beta.86+ — OpLengthLt 'length_lt' confirmed in /processor/rule/expression/types.go alongside OpLengthEq and OpLengthGt.
metadata.triples_substitution_requires: semstreams beta.86 (#155 / ADR-048 PR 4) — $entity.triple.<predicate>.triples substitution. The journal of prior execute loop IDs renders as a JSON array string inlined into the propose prompt; persona prose teaches the JSON-parse pattern.
metadata.soft_plateau_path: Plateau-N as a HARD stop is deferred (open substrate question #1). The propose persona MAY soft-recommend stop via decide(needs_clarification) when it observes plateau in the journal; the recovery rule routes to coordinator, which can respond_direct with the current state. Soft path because the LLM is the plateau judge, not the substrate.
